matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before consent, and the policy states no retention period
matrix.reasoning: Google Analytics (US) receives usage data, device ID and IP address, and network evidence shows its request firing before any consent interaction on the site, which engages the terminal-equipment rules (PECR reg. 6(1)). In the UK, the analytics exception in PECR Schedule A1 para. 5 may apply only if the information is used solely for statistical purposes to improve the service, is not shared beyond that, and users get clear information plus a simple, free way to object — conditions the evidence here does not show to be met, so the position is more permissive than in the EU but still uncertain. Separately, the privacy policy does not state how long personal data is kept or the criteria used, which is a possible inconsistency with Art. 13(2)(a) and, given the data points above, with the storage-limitation principle in Art. 5(1)(e).

fixes.policy_clause: We use Google Analytics to understand how our website and service are used, so that we can improve them. Google Analytics may receive usage data, a device ID and your IP address. Where we rely on the analytics exception, we use this information only for statistical purposes and do not share it with anyone else except to help us make those improvements. You can object to this at any time, free of charge, using the [objection mechanism / link], and we will stop.
fixes.code_change: In the site consent banner / tag loader, hold the Google Analytics gtag.js load (https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-LQ01D3PKKN) until either consent is given or the analytics exception is relied on and the user has not objected; expose a simple, free objection control that stops the tag from loading.

fixes.policy_clause: We keep personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy. The retention periods we apply are: [category of personal data] — [retention period]; [category of personal data] — [retention period]. Where we cannot set a fixed period, we decide how long to keep data using these criteria: [criteria].

matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before any consent interaction on the site
matrix.reasoning: Network evidence shows the site requests Google Analytics (US) — which receives usage data, device ID and IP address — before any consent interaction. Under s. 225, a possible inconsistency with consumer protection would arise if visitors are not clearly informed about this analytics and given a simple way to object, since the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 may allow analytics used solely for statistical purposes to run without consent only where that information and objection route exist. The same evidence is treated more strictly in the EU, so UK-specific conditions must hold for the analytics to be unproblematic here.

fixes.policy_clause: We use Google Analytics, provided by Google LLC in the United States, to understand how our site is used. It receives usage data, a device ID and your IP address, and it may run before you interact with any consent banner. We use it only for statistical purposes to improve our service. You can object to this analytics at any time by [method of objection], and [retention period] applies.
fixes.code_change: In the site's consent/analytics bootstrap, do not load https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-LQ01D3PKKN until after the consent/objection interaction, or block it until the user has been shown the analytics notice and given the objection route; the initial gtag request must not fire on page load.

matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before any consent interaction, before consent is collected
matrix.reasoning: Network evidence shows a request to Google Analytics (googletagmanager.com) loading before any consent interaction on the site, and it receives usage data, device ID and IP address. Where such storage or access is not strictly necessary to provide a service the user requested, this points to a possible inconsistency with Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3), and the absence of a prior consent basis points to a possible inconsistency with Regulation Art. 6(1) and Art. 7 on demonstrating consent. The privacy policy says nothing about how long personal data is kept, which points to a possible inconsistency with the information duty in Regulation Art. 13(2)(a) and the storage limitation principle in Art. 5(1)(e).

fixes.policy_clause: We use Google Analytics to understand how our site and product are used. Google Analytics may set cookies and receive your usage data, device ID and IP address. We only load Google Analytics after you have given consent through our cookie banner, and you can withdraw that consent at any time through the same banner.
fixes.code_change: In the site's analytics bootstrap (the gtag/js loader for G-LQ01D3PKKN), do not inject the Google Analytics script on page load. Load it only after the consent state is set to granted by the consent manager, and keep the default consent state as denied.

fixes.policy_clause: We keep personal data only for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy. Specifically: [data category] is kept for [retention period]; where a fixed period is not possible, we decide retention based on [criteria used to determine the period].

matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before any consent interaction on the site
matrix.reasoning: Network evidence shows a request to Google Analytics (US) — sending usage data, device ID and IP address — loading from googletagmanager.com before the visitor has interacted with any consent notice. Because analytics trackers run before any consent interaction, the practice may fall short of the professional diligence expected of a trader toward the average consumer, which is the possible inconsistency with Art. 5. Whether Art. 5 is engaged depends on whether the practice materially distorts, or is likely to materially distort, the average consumer's economic behaviour; a pre-consent analytics load that shapes the information the consumer sees could meet that condition. This is a compliance observation, not legal advice.

fixes.policy_clause: We load Google Analytics, a product analytics service provided by Google (US), only after you have given consent. Until then, Google Analytics does not receive your usage data, device ID or IP address. When you consent, Google Analytics processes this data on our behalf to help us understand how our site is used; you can withdraw your consent at any time in our cookie settings.
fixes.code_change: In the tag loading logic that injects https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js (the Google Analytics/gtag snippet), gate the script injection behind the consent state: do not insert the gtag script until the visitor has actively accepted analytics cookies, and remove/disable the tag when consent is withdrawn.

fixes.policy_clause: You can accept or refuse analytics cookies, including Google Analytics, before any analytics script is loaded, and refusing has the same effect as never giving consent. We show the choice before any such script runs and record your decision.
fixes.code_change: Add a consent gate/await check before any analytics initialization so the gtag request is blocked on first page load; add a test that asserts no request to googletagmanager.com occurs before the consent event fires.

matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before any consent interaction and no retention period is stated
matrix.reasoning: Network evidence shows Google Analytics (US) loading on the site before any consent interaction, receiving usage data, device ID and IP address; under Art. 7 collection generally requires the subject's consent, so this is a possible inconsistency unless a legal exception applies. Because consent is only as good as what it covers, the missing retention period also touches Art. 8(4), which requires consent to state its validity period and whether data is transferred to third parties or across borders. The policy does not state how long personal data is kept or the criteria used, which is a possible inconsistency with Art. 12(2), under which the retention period follows from when the collection purposes are achieved and data must be held in Kazakhstan.

fixes.policy_clause: We use Google Analytics to understand how our site and product are used. It may receive usage data, device ID and IP address. Where required, we ask for your consent before these tools are loaded, and you can withdraw it at any time. Because Google Analytics is operated from the United States, this involves a cross-border transfer; we ask for your consent to that transfer separately. We keep personal data only until the purposes for which it was collected are achieved, and in any case no longer than [retention period], after which it is deleted or anonymised. Personal data collected in Kazakhstan is stored in databases located in Kazakhstan.
fixes.code_change: Load Google Analytics (gtag.js / G-LQ01D3PKKN) only after the visitor's consent has been recorded, e.g. gate the script injection in the layout that currently requests https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js on page load.

fixes.policy_clause: When we ask for your consent we tell you what it covers: the list of data we collect, how long the consent is valid, whether your data may be shared with third parties, and whether it is transferred outside Kazakhstan.

matrix.headline: Google Analytics fires before consent, sending usage data, device ID and IP address
matrix.reasoning: Network evidence shows a request to Google Analytics (gtag) on the site before any consent interaction, transmitting usage data, device ID and IP address. Because collection starts before the consumer is given any notice or choice, this is a possible inconsistency with Art. 10 (Consumer right to information), which gives consumers the right to full, reliable and timely information. Kazakhstan has no cookie-specific rule, so the general consent and information requirements apply; the condition that would resolve the issue is that the analytics tag is loaded only after the consumer has been informed and has acted.

fixes.policy_clause: We use Google Analytics to understand how our website and app are used. Google Analytics receives usage data, your device ID and your IP address. We load Google Analytics only after you have been shown information about this and have given your consent; if you do not consent, Google Analytics does not run.
fixes.code_change: Gate the Google Analytics tag in the site/app bootstrap: do not inject or fire https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js until the consent flag is set (e.g. move the gtag snippet behind the consent state or use Consent Mode default 'denied' before any consent interaction).

fixes.policy_clause: You can withdraw your consent to Google Analytics at any time, and we will stop loading it and delete the analytics data linked to your device ID and IP address [within the retention period].
fixes.code_change: Add a consent-withdrawal handler that removes the gtag script, clears the _ga/_gid cookies and calls gtag('consent', 'update', {analytics_storage: 'denied'}).

UK-PECR-6.instrument: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (PECR)
UK-PECR-6.ref: reg. 6(1), as substituted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 112
UK-PECR-6.title: Storing or accessing information on a user's device
UK-PECR-6.summary: A person must not store information, or gain access to information stored, in a user's terminal equipment unless an exception in Schedule A1 applies (for example consent, or strict necessity).

UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.instrument: PECR Schedule A1, inserted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 Sch. 12
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.title: Statistical-purposes exception for analytics cookies
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.summary: Consent is not required where the sole purpose of the storage or access is to collect information for statistical purposes about how the service or website is used, with a view to improving it, provided the information is not shared with anyone else except to help make those improvements, the user is given clear and comprehensive information about the purpose, and the user is given a simple, free means of objecting and does not object.

UK-GDPR-13-2-a.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-2-a.title: Retention period must be stated
UK-GDPR-13-2-a.summary: The controller must state the period for which personal data will be stored or the criteria used to determine that period.

UK-GDPR-5-1-e.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-5-1-e.title: Storage limitation
UK-GDPR-5-1-e.summary: Personal data must be kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

UK-DMCC-225.instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 1
UK-DMCC-225.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
UK-DMCC-225.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited, including misleading actions, misleading omissions and practices that contravene professional diligence.

EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.instrument: Directive 2002/58/EC (ePrivacy Directive), as amended by Directive 2009/136/EC
EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.title: Consent for cookies and similar technologies
EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.summary: Storing information, or accessing information stored, on a user's device is only allowed with the user's consent after clear information, unless strictly necessary to provide a service the user requested.

EU-GDPR-7.title: Conditions for consent
EU-GDPR-7.summary: Where processing relies on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate that the person consented, and consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give.

EU-GDPR-6.title: Lawful basis for processing
EU-GDPR-6.summary: Processing is lawful only if at least one legal basis applies, such as consent, contract, legal obligation or legitimate interests.

EU-GDPR-5-1-e.title: Storage limitation
EU-GDPR-5-1-e.summary: Personal data must be kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

EU-GDPR-13-2-a.title: Retention period must be stated
EU-GDPR-13-2-a.summary: The controller must state the period for which personal data will be stored or, if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period.

EU-UCPD-5.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
EU-UCPD-5.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited: practices contrary to professional diligence that materially distort, or are likely to materially distort, the economic behaviour of the average consumer.

KZ-PD-7.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-7.title: Conditions for collection and processing
KZ-PD-7.summary: Collection and processing of personal data is carried out with the consent of the subject, except in cases set by law. Transfer to third parties and cross-border transfer are subject to consent.

KZ-PD-8.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-8.title: Required content of consent
KZ-PD-8.summary: Consent must state, among other things, its validity period, whether data may be transferred to third parties, whether cross-border transfer takes place, and the list of data collected.

KZ-PD-12-2.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-12-2.title: Storage in Kazakhstan and retention period
KZ-PD-12-2.summary: Personal data must be stored in a database or digital facility located in the territory of Kazakhstan. The retention period is set by the date the purposes of collection and processing are achieved.

KZ-CP-10.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 274-IV 'On Protection of Consumer Rights' (4 May 2010)
KZ-CP-10.title: Consumer right to information
KZ-CP-10.summary: The consumer has the right to receive full, reliable and timely information about goods, works and services and about the seller or provider.
